risks.title: Tariffs and international trade
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to tariffs (Section 232 on steel, reciprocal tariffs) and trade measures that create significant uncertainty regarding their scope, duration and financial impact. Tariffs could reduce consumer demand and materially impact consolidated operating results. While the company has mitigated certain impacts through expanded metallurgical margins, potential invalidation, modification or expansion of tariffs could have material negative effects.

risks.title: Antidumping and countervailing duties litigation
risks.score_rationale: The company is involved in complex litigation concerning antidumping and countervailing duty orders on mattresses from China, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey and Vietnam. The DOC has imposed antidumping and countervailing duties of 2% to 763% (effective through May 2026) and extended the order on Chinese mattresses with duties up to 1,732% through May 2030. An ongoing appeal before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit regarding Indonesia creates significant legal uncertainty that could affect costs, margins and results.

risks.title: Increased competition and low-priced products
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to increased competition in the mattress and furniture segments, with foreign manufacturers from Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey and Vietnam selling products at lower prices, which could impact volumes, sales and gross margins. Tariffs have partially mitigated this competitive pressure, but a reduction in tariffs could exacerbate the issue.

risks.title: Critical infrastructure and operational dependencies
risks.score_rationale: The company is heavily dependent on three critical facilities for the production of steel wire for mattress springs: the steel wire mill in Sterling, Illinois (annual capacity of approximately 500,000 tons) and drawing mills in Carthage, Missouri and Kouts, Indiana. These facilities are central to the Bedding Products segment. A disruption to these operations or scrap supply could require the purchase of steel wire from alternative sources and could have a material negative impact on operating results.

risks.title: Cash position and elevated debt levels
risks.score_rationale: The company reduced its debt by $366 million through the sale of the Aerospace Products group ($280M net proceeds, $91M gain) in August 2025, but maintains total debt of $1,498 million (2025). While declining, the current debt level represents a significant debt service burden and could limit financial flexibility for future investments, acquisitions or shareholder distributions. In July 2025, the company amended its credit agreement to extend maturity to 2030 and reduce loan commitments from $1.2 billion to $1.0 billion.

ai_positioning.summary: LEG does not mention artificial intelligence, machine learning or related technologies in its 10-K report for fiscal year 2025. No strategic, operational or technological reference to AI is present.
